s1: Interaction probability vs gamma energy: NOT shown — only one gamma energy has been simulated. Run ./run_all.sh --archive <tag> at other energies.
s2: Light yield is a configured INPUT. The generated photon number per event is an OUTPUT of the stochastic model and equals yield × deposited energy only on average.

s5: The energy resolution is dominated by position-dependent optical collection (spread 6.4%), not by photoelectron counting (≈1.2%). Changing reflector, surface finish, sensor size/position or absorption length will change it strongly.

Photopeak efficiency uses the window μ ± FWHM minus a fitted linear background; the truth full-energy fraction in Section 3 is an upper bound. They differ when the peak is broad or non-Gaussian (depth-dependent light collection produces a low-side tail).
The full-energy peak is clearly asymmetric (skewness +0.53), so a Gaussian FWHM is only approximate. Compare the fitted value with the truth-tagged value and inspect the spectrum plot.
Signal linearity: NOT evaluated — it needs simulations at several gamma energies (run ./run_all.sh --archive <tag> for each energy).

photopeak.method: Gaussian + linear background fit to the full spectrum
